newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index plunges in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index plunges in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell sharply in early Thursday morning trade, unsettled by pre-New Year weakness on Wall Street, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index 161 points to 13,290 at the open, then fell further to 13,214 in the first few minutes of trade.
But turnover was low at less than HK$400 million.
"This is due very much to the 100-point fall on Wall Street," said David Williamson, director at W.I. Carr. "But this looks like an overreaction."
Properties led the market down, falling 2.0 percent compared with the blue chip index's 1.2 percent.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings took the greatest beating, shedding HK$2.00 to HK$163.50. Hang Seng Bank followed with a loss of HK$1.75 to HK$92.25.
"This weakness should be short-lived," Williamson added.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 101.10 or 1.54 percent to 6,448.27 and the S&P 500 lost more than 13 points on Tuesday but on very thin volume, brokers said.
The falls were precipitated by U.S. economic data showed greater than expected home sales and consumer confidence, suggesting the U.S. economy would grow at a faster, more inflationary rate in 1997.
Hang Seng Index futures were also greatest marked down. The December contract was trading 220 points down at 13,240 after 20 minutes of trade and the February 255 at 13,255.
Technical indicators turned mixed, analysts said.
"Relative strength and the MACD (moving average convergence divergence) have both turned down," said Alex Wong, analyst at Dharmala Securities.
"Short-term support lies at 13,100," said Wong, adding that if the index breaks below this level, the next brake may be at 12,800 -12,900.
"If we fall below 13,100, we could see a long period of consolidation in a big range," said Wong. His range lies between 12,800 and 13,500.
